chief_complaint: pain over outer elbow and forearm weakness when gripping objects, lifting coffee mugs, or turning doorknobs with positive Cozen test
hpi_details: 44F carpenter presenting with exquisite tenderness at the lateral epicondyle origin of the extensor carpi radialis brevis (ECRB) treated with counterforce elbow bracing, wrist extensor eccentric strengthening physical therapy, and ergonomic tool modification.
ideas: She thinks she strained a tendon or bruised a joint from the constant vibration of power drills and hammering on the job.
concerns: She is worried that her failing grip will cause her to drop power tools on the job site, injuring herself and losing carpentry contracts.
expectations: She hopes to be fitted with an elbow support band and given immediate pain relief so she can grip her tools tomorrow.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Lateral Epicondylitis Tennis Elbow Tendinopathy.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.

dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Severe progressive motor deficit.

must_ask.say: Did the elbow pain start after repetitive gripping or wrist movements at work or with tools?
Is the pain over the outside of your elbow, and does it get worse when you grip or lift things?
Does the pain get worse when you try to bend your wrist backward against resistance?
How much is this limiting everyday tasks like holding a mug or turning a doorknob?
Have you tried a brace, physical therapy, or any other treatment for this so far?

history.answer: My right outer elbow has been hurting for about two months, and my grip feels weak whenever I try to hold things.
The pain is strictly on the outside bump of my right elbow, and it only affects this one elbow. My left arm is completely fine.
It started gradually about eight weeks ago after a big carpentry job, and it has slowly become more persistent.
It feels like a sharp, burning ache right on the bone, usually about a 4 out of 10 at rest, but it shoots up to a 7 or 8 when I use my tools.
No, there has not been any swelling, redness, or heat around the joint.
I feel a little stiffness first thing in the morning for maybe five minutes, but it loosens right up once I move my arm.
Gripping my hammer, turning screwdrivers, lifting heavy mugs, or twisting doorknobs makes it much worse. Resting my arm helps ease the ache.
It makes my carpentry work tough because my grip gives out when lifting planks, and I have trouble lifting a filled coffee mug or turning door handles. Walking and stairs are fine.
No, I never had a sudden fall, direct blow, or loud pop in the elbow. It just came on from repetitive hammering and drilling.
No, I have never had pain or trouble like this in my elbow before.
No, I do not have any fever, chills, night sweats, or fatigue.
No, I have not felt unusually tired or lost any weight.
No rashes, scaly skin patches, mouth sores, hair loss, or red irritated eyes.
No, my back feels fine in the morning, and I do not have any heel soreness or swollen sausage fingers.
No diarrhea, no pain when urinating, no discharge, and no sore throat recently.
I do not drink alcohol, I eat a regular balanced diet, and I do not take water pills.
I have never taken steroid pills or immune medications, and I have never had any injections or operations on this joint.
I have been in a faithful monogamous relationship with my husband for twelve years, with no other partners.
Yes, whenever I bend my wrist backward against resistance, like lifting something with my palm facing down, it shoots sharp pain right to the outside of my elbow.
No, I do not have any numbness, pins and needles, or shooting electrical pain down into my fingers or forearm.
No, my neck feels completely normal with no stiffness, aching, or pain shooting into my shoulder.
I tried taking over-the-counter ibuprofen and resting it for a few days, but the pain came right back as soon as I went back to work.
I thought I strained a tendon or bruised a joint from using the hammer and impact drill all week on the job site.
I'm really worried that my grip will suddenly give out while holding a power saw on a ladder and I'll get kicked off the crew.
I was hoping to get one of those tight forearm bands and something for the ache so I can hold my tools without dropping them tomorrow.
I have always been healthy and have no history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or arthritis.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I am not taking any prescription medications, vitamins, or supplements.
I do not have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I work full-time as a finish carpenter, doing a lot of repetitive gripping and hand-tool work, and I live at home with my husband.
No one in my family has rheumatoid arthritis, gout, or autoimmune joint disorders.
My last period started two weeks ago. My cycles are regular every 28 days, my husband has had a vasectomy, and there is no chance of pregnancy.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.6°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.

No swelling, erythema, warmth, or deformity of either elbow. Full active and passive range of motion of both elbows, but exquisite localized tenderness on palpation over the right lateral epicondyle. Positive Cozen test on the right with reproduced lateral epicondyle pain during resisted wrist extension.

Pain provoked over the right lateral epicondyle with resisted wrist extension and resisted middle finger extension; motor strength in wrist flexion, elbow flexion, elbow extension, and hand grip otherwise 5/5 bilaterally without focal motor deficit.
Normal light touch and pinprick sensation over bilateral upper extremities, including C6, C7, and superficial radial nerve distributions.
Biceps, brachioradialis, and triceps deep tendon reflexes 2+ and symmetric bilaterally.
Full active cervical spine range of motion without pain, no cervical paraspinal tenderness, and Spurling test is negative bilaterally.
No skin rashes, psoriasis plaques, nail changes, or tophi observed anywhere on the upper extremities.
